title: Uniaxial stress effects on magnetic and electric properties of the ground state in a centrosymmetric magnetic skyrmion host Gd$_2$PdSi$_3$
authors: Hiraku Saito, Naoki Kobayashi, Takuro Kawasaki, Tatsuya Nakamura, Akiko Kikkawa, Yasujiro Taguchi, Yoshinori Tokura, Taro Nakajima
abstract: We investigate effects of uniaxial stress to magnetic orders and electrical resistivity of the centrosymmetric magnetic skyrmion compound Gd$_2$PdSi$_3$, which has a hexagonal crystal structure composed of triangular lattice layers of magnetic Gd$^{3+}$ ions. This compound is known to exhibit the triple-$q$ magnetic skyrmion lattice phase with a giant topological Hall effect in the first field induced phase [T. Kurumaji $\textit{et al}$. Science $\textbf{365}$, 914-918 (2019)]. In contrast to the established picture of the field-induced phase, the ground state of this system still remains to be studied. Although previous studies reported the existence of the incommensurate magnetic modulations described by a magnetic modulation wave vector ${\bf q}=(q,0,0)$ where $q\sim 0.14$ and its equivalents, it is still unclear whether the magnetic structure is a single-$q$ structure or a multiple-$q$ structure. In the present study, we performed magnetization, resistivity and neutron diffraction measurements with a compressive uniaxial stress applied perpendicular to the $c$ axis. The observed data revealed that the system did not exhibit anisotropic magnetic and electric properties expected from a single-$q$ magnetic order, suggesting that the magnetic ground state of this system is a multi-$q$ magnetic order.
summary: This work investigates the ground state magnetic order of $	ext{Gd}_2	ext{PdSi}_3$ by applying uniaxial stress while measuring its magnetotransport and diffraction properties. By observing that the system's response does not match predictions for a single-wavevector ($\mathbf{q}$) structure, the authors conclude that the material possesses a multi-$\mathbf{q}$ magnetic order. This provides critical insight into the complex magnetic ground states of skyrmion hosts.
main_problem: The study investigates how uniaxial stress affects the magnetic and electrical properties of the ground state in the centrosymmetric skyrmion host $	ext{Gd}_2	ext{PdSi}_3$, specifically aiming to distinguish between single-$\mathbf{q}$ and multi-$\mathbf{q}$ magnetic ordering.
main_result: The experimental data, particularly neutron diffraction measurements under stress, strongly suggest that the ground state ($	ext{IC-1}$ phase) is a robust multi-$\mathbf{q}$ magnetic order, ruling out a single-$\mathbf{q}$ structure.
method: Measurements included magnetization and resistivity under applied uniaxial stress, complemented by polarized neutron diffraction to probe the magnetic structure.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{Gd}_2	ext{PdSi}_3$, a hexagonal crystal with triangular layers of $	ext{Gd}^{3+}$ ions known for hosting skyrmion phases. The investigation focuses on resolving the ambiguity between single-$\mathbf{q}$ and multi-$\mathbf{q}$ magnetic ground states.
key_observables: Magnetization ($\Delta M$), resistivity difference ($\Deltaho$), and intensities of multiple magnetic Bragg reflections (e.g., six reflections around $(1, 0, 0)$).
important_parameters: Uniaxial stress ($\sigma$) applied perpendicular to the $c$-axis (up to $200 	ext{ MPa}$); temperature ($T$); and magnetic field ($\mu_0	ext{H}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that anisotropic properties expected from a single-$\mathbf{q}$ order would manifest differently under stress compared to the observed results.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams, temperature dependence of $\Delta M$ and $\Deltaho$, and crucially, neutron diffraction intensity maps showing multiple magnetic reflections persisting even when uniaxial stress is applied.
paper_structure: The paper establishes background context on skyrmion phases in $	ext{Gd}_2	ext{PdSi}_3$, details the application of uniaxial stress measurements (M, $ho$, Neutron Diffraction), presents results showing lack of single-$\mathbf{q}$ anisotropy, and concludes that a multi-$\mathbf{q}$ order is necessary to explain the observations.
why_interesting: The study uses external mechanical strain ($\sigma$) as a powerful tuning parameter to probe fundamental symmetries and magnetic ordering types (single vs. multiple wave vectors) in topological magnets, which has parallels with controlling quantum states via external fields.

Figure 2(a) shows the temperature dependence of the mag- netization M in a magnetic ﬁeld of 0.01 T applied parallel to the [100] direction. At ambient pressure, the magnetiza- tion is suppressed and start decreasing below at around 22 K, which corresponds to the phase transition from paramagnetic (PM) phase to the IC-2 phase, TN1. Gd2PdSi3 undergoes the magnetic transition to IC-1 at TN2. According to the previous studies, the phase transition at TN2 results in a local maximum in the magnetization along the c axis [3, 15], while no clear anomaly is observed in the a-axis magnetization. The present results are well consistent with the previous result.
